args.summary: The latest production deploy of checkout-api (v2.3.1) failed health checks with an 18% error rate in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). Per the platform runbook, checkout-api was rolled back to the most recent release that was healthy in production, v2.3.0. The first rollback attempt only completed in us-east before the orchestrator halted (partial failure); a retry completed the rollout to us-west and eu-west. Final state: v2.3.0 deployed in all regions, service healthy, error rate ~0.2%. v2.3.1 should not be redeployed until root cause of the health-check failures is identified.

trace.final:
All done. Summary of what I did:

1. **Diagnosed the issue**: checkout-api v2.3.1 (the latest deploy) was failing health checks with an 18% error rate across all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). The deployment history showed v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production.

2. **Rolled back to v2.3.0 in all regions**: The first rollback attempt partially failed (it completed in us-east, then the orchestrator halted). I verified the state, retried, and the rollout completed. Confirmed all three regions are now on v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate has dropped to ~0.2%.

3. **Opened SEV2 incident INC-0001** (on-call has been paged): "checkout-api rollback from v2.3.1 to v2.3.0 after failed health checks," documenting the failed deploy, the partial rollback failure and retry, the final healthy state, and a note that v2.3.1 should not be redeployed until root cause is identified.
